run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-14T20:37:45Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is driven by frontend-proxy's own error spans: over 19:37:45Z-20:58:11Z it recorded 28.36 ERROR `ingress` spans and 6.08 ERROR `router frontend egress` spans, and its 5-minute ingress error rate was nonzero in most buckets (0.0037-0.0148/s), peaking at 0.0333/s at 20:32:45 and 0.0312/s at 20:34:45, with 0.0074-0.0077/s again at 20:38:45 and 20:50:45 - the same magnitude as the alert's stated 0.0111/s. The frontend-proxy access log shows those responses as `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` against the `frontend` upstream cluster, repeatedly from 20:07:39 through 20:45:50 on paths such as `/`, `/api/products/<id>`, `/api/cart` and `/api/recommendations`, with 95-byte error bodies and 98-715 ms durations. In the one failed request inspected end-to-end (trace b303e7616d6cc9296844951cbe4749d5) the egress span has http.status_code=0 and there is no frontend span at all, i.e. the frontend upstream never started or never answered the request; therefore the immediate cause sits on the frontend side of the proxy hop, not in a downstream service the proxy calls. Why the frontend terminates connections without responding is NOT established: frontend container logs could not be read, and Jaeger holds no traces after ~20:25. Candidate contributors kept open are chronic frontend CPU throttling (100m limit, 21-35% of CFS periods throttled all window), a keep-alive/idle-connection race between Envoy and the frontend HTTP server, and the frontend's own error burst at 20:30-20:35 that coincides with the product-catalog pod replacement at 20:30:20-20:30:24 (correlation only; the 503s already existed 18+ minutes earlier, so the rollout cannot be the sole trigger). The flagd config has productCatalogFailure set to `on`, but no product-catalog ERROR span was returned, so its effect is unverified.

claims.text: For service_name=frontend-proxy the only error-bearing span names in 19:37:45Z-20:58:11Z are `ingress` (STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase 28.36 spans) and `router frontend egress` (6.08 spans); its status_code label values are STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET and its span names are exactly `ingress` (server) and `router frontend egress` (client).

frontend-proxy's 5-minute ingress ERROR-span rate was nonzero in most steps of the window: 0.0080-0.0148/s from 20:10:45 to 20:26:45, 0.0185/s at 20:28:45, peak 0.0333/s at 20:32:45 and 0.0312/s at 20:34:45, then 0 at 20:36:45, 0.0074/s at 20:38:45 and 20:40:45, 0 at 20:42:45, and 0.0037-0.0111/s at 20:44:45-20:50:45 (0.0077/s at 20:50:45); this is the same order of magnitude as the 0.0111/s in the alert annotation.

frontend-proxy access logs record the failing responses verbatim as `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` against upstream cluster `frontend`, with 95 bytes returned and durations 98-715 ms, at 20:07:39.947 (GET /), 20:07:40.142 (GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N), 20:11:30.645 and 20:11:30.746 (GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N, GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO), 20:26:22.036 (GET /api/products/0PUK6V6EV0), 20:28:12.789 (GET /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4), 20:30:20.360 (GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP), 20:31:14.331 (GET /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4), 20:41:36.983 (GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N), 20:45:04.908 (GET /api/cart), 20:45:50.003 (GET /api/recommendations?productIds=HQTGWGPNH4) and 20:45:50.621 (GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP).

In the sampled frontend-proxy error traces (trace times 20:07:39.946-20:25:24.121) every failed request pairs a frontend-proxy `ingress` span with error=true, http.status_code=503 and otel.status_code=ERROR with a `router frontend egress` span carrying error="true" and http.status_code="0", and the corresponding load-generator `GET` span also records 503/ERROR (12 such ingress/egress/load-generator triples).

Full trace b303e7616d6cc9296844951cbe4749d5 (started 20:18:10, spans_omitted 0, spans_outside_window 0) contains only 4 spans: load-generator `user_browse_product`, load-generator `GET` (503/ERROR), frontend-proxy `ingress` (503/ERROR) and frontend-proxy `router frontend egress` (error="true", http.status_code="0", 953,816 us). No span of service `frontend` exists in that trace.

Window-wide ERROR-span increases across all services are: frontend-proxy ingress 28.36, frontend-proxy `router frontend egress` 6.08, frontend `GET` 5.06, frontend `POST` 1.01, frontend `POST /api/checkout` 1.01, frontend `executing api route (pages) /api/checkout` 1.01, frontend `tcp.connect` 1.01, ad `flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream` 3.05, fraud-detection `flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream` 3.04 and recommendation `/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream` 4.05; the same query returned explicit zero-valued ERROR series for frontend's gRPC client spans, accounting `orders receive`, payment `GET`/`dns.lookup`/`tcp.connect`, ad `ResolveBoolean` and fraud-detection `ResolveInt`. No ERROR series at all was returned for cart, checkout, currency, shipping, email, product-catalog, quote, image-provider or kafka.

frontend's own ERROR spans are confined to two 5-minute buckets, 20:32:45 and 20:34:45: `GET` 0.0185/s and 0.0195/s, and `POST`, `POST /api/checkout`, `executing api route (pages) /api/checkout` and `tcp.connect` 0.0037-0.0039/s; both buckets are 0 in every other step from 20:08:45 to 20:50:45, so the frontend error burst ran roughly 20:30-20:35.

product-catalog was rolled out inside the window: pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 was Scheduled/Created/Started 20:30:20-20:30:23 while pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp was Stopping/Deleted at 20:30:24, with ReplicaSet product-catalog-55f64b54c9 scaled 0->1 and product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc scaled 1->0; the image in the event is unchanged (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog). These 9 Kubernetes events are the only events in namespace otel-demo inside the window, and none names frontend or frontend-proxy.

At query time (20:58) all 21 otel-demo deployments had replicas=1, readyReplicas=1 and availableReplicas=1, and all 21 pods were Running, ready=true with restartCount 0, including frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw (started 2026-11-14T19:57:18Z) and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-mzj56 (started 19:57:19Z), running ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend and ...:2.1.3-frontend-proxy.

The frontend container is configured with resources limits cpu=100m, memory=200Mi and requests cpu=50m, memory=100Mi, and has no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe; the frontend-proxy container has limits cpu=30m, memory=50Mi and requests cpu=15m, memory=25Mi. Both deployments are RollingUpdate with maxSurge/maxUnavailable 25%.

Over the whole window the frontend container's working-set memory peaked at 130,908,160 bytes (~125 MiB), below its 200Mi limit, and frontend-proxy's peaked at 21,143,552 bytes (~20 MiB) against its 50Mi limit.

The frontend container's CPU usage stayed at 0.032-0.052 cores per 2-minute step (limit 0.1 core) between 20:07:45 and 20:47:45, while its CFS throttling ratio was 0.21-0.35 in every step and 0.284 over the whole window; frontend-proxy's whole-window throttling ratio was 0.038.

The live flagd configuration for the demo sets productCatalogFailure defaultVariant to `on` (state ENABLED, variants off=false/on=true); all other flags (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, recommendationCacheFailure) have defaultVariant `off`.

The trace backend used by the trace tools is served by jaeger-traces-recorder-0 (namespace data-recorders, started 20:13:03) and jaeger-collector-7bc97cc4bc-fnrp9 (namespace opentelemetry-collectors, started 20:05:25), and the frontend-proxy error traces returned cover only 20:07:39.946949Z-20:25:24.121477Z; a traces_search for service frontend over 20:30:00-20:40:00 returned no traces.

A frontend pod crash, restart or OOM is not supported: both deployments are 1/1 ready/available, frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-mzj56 show restartCount 0 and ready=true, frontend memory peaked at ~125 MiB against a 200Mi limit, and no OOMKilled, Evicted or Unhealthy event exists in namespace otel-demo for the window (the only events are the product-catalog rollout).

The frontend CPU throttling ratio did not spike around the 20:32-20:35 error peak or the alert time: per-2-minute values stayed between 0.21 and 0.35 from 20:07:45 through 20:47:45 (e.g. 0.258 at 20:07:45, 0.333 at 20:34:45, 0.272 at 20:38:45, 0.323 at 20:50:45), so a throttling step-change is not observable.

An enabled productCatalogFailure flag did not produce observable product-catalog failures in this window: no ERROR series was returned for service_name=product-catalog, and frontend's client span `grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct` has an explicit 0 ERROR increase over the window.

Rejected as the sole trigger of this alert: the product-catalog pod replacement at 20:30:20-20:30:24. frontend-proxy was already logging identical 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses at 20:07:39.947, 20:07:40.142 and 20:11:30.645/20:11:30.746, more than 18 minutes before the rollout, and its error rate was nonzero in the 20:10:45-20:30:45 steps as well as after the rollout.

Immediate cause of the alert: the single `frontend` upstream terminates the proxied HTTP connection before any response is started, so frontend-proxy answers 503 and its `ingress`/`router frontend egress` spans are marked ERROR. Support: the response-code detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on the `frontend` cluster, and failed trace b303e7616d6cc9296844951cbe4749d5, which has an egress span with http.status_code=0 and no frontend span at all. The frontend-side reason (what closes the socket) is not established from the available evidence.

Candidate mechanism still open: an idle/keep-alive connection reuse race between frontend-proxy (Envoy) and the frontend HTTP server - the frontend closes a pooled connection while Envoy is sending a request on it, producing connection_termination with no frontend span. It fits the sporadic occurrence on all paths from 20:07 onward and the 100-200 ms paired failures (20:07:39.947/20:07:40.142, 20:11:30.645/20:11:30.746, 20:45:50.003/20:45:50.621), but the observed egress durations of 98-954 ms are longer than an immediate stale-socket reset would normally take, so it is unconfirmed.

Candidate contributing factor: the frontend is chronically CPU-constrained at its 100m limit (usage ~0.032-0.052 cores, 21-35% of CFS periods throttled every step, 28.4% over the window), which can delay or abort its HTTP handling and make it miss the proxy's expectations. Because the throttling is steady rather than coincident with the 20:32-20:35 peak, its causal role in the 503s is unproven.

Candidate for the 20:30-20:35 frontend-only error burst (GET 5.06, POST/POST /api/checkout/executing api route /api/checkout/tcp.connect 1.01 each): loss or reset of the frontend's connections to product-catalog when product-catalog's pod was replaced at 20:30:20-20:30:24 could have failed those in-flight requests (including one `tcp.connect` ERROR and one checkout route failure). This is timing correlation only: frontend errors are confined to the 20:32:45 and 20:34:45 buckets and the rollout happens at 20:30:20, but no trace covers 20:30-20:35 and frontend container logs could not be read.

Candidate not confirmed: the enabled productCatalogFailure flag (`on` in flagd-config) as the injected fault behind this alert. It could only explain errors on product-catalog reads, whereas the alert is driven by frontend-proxy 503 connection-termination spans that carry no frontend span at all, and neither product-catalog ERROR spans nor frontend grpc GetProduct ERROR spans were observed in the window.

Obtain the frontend application's stdout/stderr for 20:07-20:58 (or enable logging) to identify what closes the inbound HTTP connection; frontend container logs returned no readable lines for the window, so this is the single most valuable missing artifact.

Compare the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream cluster keep-alive/idle timeout for the `frontend` cluster with the frontend HTTP server's keepAliveTimeout, and consider retries for idempotent GET paths, to test the keep-alive race hypothesis.

Raise the frontend container CPU limit above 100m (it runs at ~0.05 core with 21-35% CFS throttling and no probes) and confirm whether throttling relief reduces the 503 rate; also review why the RequestErrorRate rule fires on any rate above 0 (0.0111/s here), which makes it sensitive to single failed requests.

gaps: The frontend container produced no readable log lines in 19:37:45Z-20:58:11Z (fetch_pod_logs returned status no_data with 0 lines for both the 19:37-20:58 and 20:28-20:40 windows), so the application-side reason the frontend terminates connections cannot be verified.

Jaeger trace coverage is limited to about 20:07:39-20:25:24 for the frontend-proxy error traces; traces_search for service frontend over 20:30:00-20:40:00 returned no traces, so the 20:30-20:35 peak and the alert time 20:37:45 cannot be examined at span level.
frontend-proxy access-log reads stop at 20:46:49Z (no lines exist in the readable stream after that), so 503 evidence after 20:46:49 is only from span metrics, not log detail.

No alerting rules are loaded in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned no rules for rule_name RequestErrorRate and none for type=alert), so the exact alert expression/lookback and the 0.0111/s value cannot be verified from the rule definition.

change_history is not integrated into this Run, so what changed the product-catalog deployment at 20:30:20 (new ReplicaSet product-catalog-55f64b54c9, same image tag) and what set productCatalogFailure to `on` in flagd-config are unknown.

No ERROR series was returned for cart, checkout, currency, shipping, email, product-catalog, quote, image-provider or kafka, which makes their error status during the window unknown rather than zero; image-provider and kafka also have no span data in the trace sample.

It is unresolved why frontend-proxy records 28.36 ingress ERROR spans but only 6.08 `router frontend egress` ERROR spans (possibly failed egress attempts recorded without a status), so the number of failed upstream attempts is uncertain.

The product-catalog pod's logs returned no lines matching error/fail/UNAVAILABLE for 20:30:20-20:58:11 (status no_data), so whether the enabled productCatalogFailure flag caused any failed GetProduct call is unknown.
Kubernetes objects and pod states were read at query time (~20:58), after the incident; they show the current state and cannot prove pod readiness or restart counts during 20:30-20:37.
next_steps: Collect the frontend Next.js server logs (container stdout/stderr) for 20:07-20:58, including any unhandled rejection, socket hang-up or gRPC UNAVAILABLE messages.

Inspect and, if authorized, compare the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream cluster configuration (idle timeout, keep-alive, retry policy) for the `frontend` cluster against the frontend server's keepAliveTimeout.
Review the change that replaced product-catalog's ReplicaSet at 20:30:20 and the flagd productCatalogFailure setting with the change-history system (not available in this Run).
Consider raising the frontend CPU limit from 100m and adding probes, then observe whether frontend-proxy 503 UC responses and the corresponding ERROR spans stop.
If the alert's intent is to catch real user-facing errors, review the RequestErrorRate rule expression/threshold (currently firing on a rate of 0.0111/s, i.e. a handful of spans per 5 minutes).

recommendation.text: Obtain the frontend application's stdout/stderr for 20:07-20:58 (or enable logging) to identify what closes the inbound HTTP connection; frontend container logs returned no readable lines for the window, so this is the single most valuable missing artifact.

Compare the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream cluster keep-alive/idle timeout for the `frontend` cluster with the frontend HTTP server's keepAliveTimeout, and consider retries for idempotent GET paths, to test the keep-alive race hypothesis.

Raise the frontend container CPU limit above 100m (it runs at ~0.05 core with 21-35% CFS throttling and no probes) and confirm whether throttling relief reduces the 503 rate; also review why the RequestErrorRate rule fires on any rate above 0 (0.0111/s here), which makes it sensitive to single failed requests.

counter_evidence.text: A frontend pod crash, restart or OOM is not supported: both deployments are 1/1 ready/available, frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-mzj56 show restartCount 0 and ready=true, frontend memory peaked at ~125 MiB against a 200Mi limit, and no OOMKilled, Evicted or Unhealthy event exists in namespace otel-demo for the window (the only events are the product-catalog rollout).

The frontend CPU throttling ratio did not spike around the 20:32-20:35 error peak or the alert time: per-2-minute values stayed between 0.21 and 0.35 from 20:07:45 through 20:47:45 (e.g. 0.258 at 20:07:45, 0.333 at 20:34:45, 0.272 at 20:38:45, 0.323 at 20:50:45), so a throttling step-change is not observable.

An enabled productCatalogFailure flag did not produce observable product-catalog failures in this window: no ERROR series was returned for service_name=product-catalog, and frontend's client span `grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct` has an explicit 0 ERROR increase over the window.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Rejected as the sole trigger of this alert: the product-catalog pod replacement at 20:30:20-20:30:24. frontend-proxy was already logging identical 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses at 20:07:39.947, 20:07:40.142 and 20:11:30.645/20:11:30.746, more than 18 minutes before the rollout, and its error rate was nonzero in the 20:10:45-20:30:45 steps as well as after the rollout.
